report_target_store <- Sys.getenv("TRANSPLANT_TARGET_STORE", "_targets")

## Resident modeling cohort


### Purpose

Validate the six resident-model exclusions and exact model universe.

### Inputs

Maximum-duration resident AUC effects, climate context, taxonomy, and full sampling covariance.

### Decisions and exclusions

Exactly the six configured taxa are removed here and nowhere in the response stages.

### Before/after counts and validation checks

```{r}
scope <- targets::tar_read(resident_scope)
settings <- targets::tar_read(analysis_settings)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  effects = scope$effects, species = scope$species, experiments = scope$experiments
))
knitr::kable(data.frame(excluded_from_resident_models = settings$exclusions))
knitr::kable(scope$V_validation)
```

### Problems flagged

Any count, identity, covariance, ordering, or required-consistency mismatch stops this branch.

### Principal outputs

`resident_auc_data`, `resident_sampling_covariance_matrix`, and `resident_scope`.

### PASS/FAIL

The target stops unless the scope is exactly 1,604 effects, 526 species, and 42 experiments.
## Resident climate meta-regression


### Question

How does maximum-duration resident Delta AUC vary with destination temperature,
destination precipitation, and warming under the anchored random structure?

### Dataset and sample size

The validated resident cohort contains 1,604 effects, 526 species, and 42 experiments.

### Exact model specification

Fixed effects are `T_z * P_z * W_z`. Random effects are an independent species intercept, an independent species `W_z` slope, and a correlated species `T_z`/`P_z`/`TP_z` block (`GEN`).

### Assumptions

Effect estimates use the full ordered `V_auc`; CR1 clusters by experiment. Scaling is fixed before fitting.

### Convergence and covariance diagnostics

Optimizer codes, warnings, random covariance diagnostics, and all five profile-likelihood intervals are shown below.

### Main numerical results

```{r}
bundle <- targets::tar_read(resident_climate_model_results)
knitr::kable(bundle$fit_statistics)
knitr::kable(bundle$fixed)
knitr::kable(bundle$CR1)
knitr::kable(bundle$random)
knitr::kable(bundle$variance_profiles)
```

### Interpretation boundary

CR1 is clustered by experiment. The model and all five profile-likelihood
variance intervals are fitted by analytical targets; the report only reads
their returned objects.

### Principal objects

`resident_climate_model`, `resident_climate_model_results`, and `resident_climate_variance_profiles`.

### PASS/FAIL

The fitted model, covariance diagnostics, and all five variance profiles must
complete without errors or non-finite estimates.
## Species context classification


### Question

Which eligible species are consistently positive, consistently negative, or cross zero across their own observed climate support?

### Dataset and sample size

Eligible units are drawn from 526 modeled species; exact eligible counts and class counts are shown below.

### Exact model specification

Conditional coefficients come from the resident climate model. Extrema are evaluated within each species' observed destination T-P hull at the anchored median warming context.

### Assumptions

Eligibility requires at least four experiments and a full-rank within-species
climate design. Classification is evaluated only inside each eligible species'
observed climate support.

### Convergence and covariance diagnostics

This step fits no model; it inherits the resident climate model convergence and covariance gates.

### Main numerical results

```{r}
summary <- targets::tar_read(species_classification_summary)
classification <- targets::tar_read(species_classification)
examples <- targets::tar_read(species_callout_examples)
knitr::kable(summary)
knitr::kable(examples[, c("species_id", "fitted_class", "selection_rank_within_class", "selection_rule")])
knitr::kable(head(classification[order(classification$fitted_class, classification$species_id), ], 20))
```

### PASS/FAIL

Eligibility requires at least four experiments and a full-rank within-species climate design.
The four callout species are selected by the documented within-class rules and are not chosen during rendering.

### Interpretation boundary

Classes summarize fitted response over observed support; they are not the significance-based winner/loser labels from the response stage.

### Principal objects

`species_context_bundle`, `species_classification`, and `species_callout_examples`.
